citation: Lauersen JB, Andersen TE, Andersen LB (2018). Strength training as superior, dose-dependent and safe prevention of acute and overuse sports injuries: a systematic review, qualitative analysis and meta-analysis. British journal of sports medicine.
population: 7738 participants aged 12-40 years, athletes across various sports
intervention: Strength training exercises as primary prevention of sports injuries
outcome_measures: Relative risk of acute and overuse sports injuries
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of six RCTs found that strength training substantially reduces the risk of acute and overuse sports injuries. The cluster-adjusted intention-to-treat analysis showed a relative risk of 0.338, indicating a 66% reduction in injury risk, with high strength of evidence and no publication bias.
key_findings: Cluster-adjusted intention-to-treat analysis established RR 0.338 (95% CI 0.238-0.480) for strength training preventing sports injuries.
A 10% increase in strength training volume reduced the risk of injury by more than four percentage points.
The result was consistent across robustness tests and strength of evidence was high.
Formal tests found no publication bias.
Studies were generally well designed with high compliance rates and were safe.
limitations: Only six RCTs included with considerable heterogeneity in populations and interventions; abstract only limits detailed risk of bias assessment.
